assessments.reasoning: The Scala 2.13 object-definition rule associates the declared name with one object and attributes a newly defined class to that object. Both properties come from the construct's definition.

challenge.method: Check whether the template syntax extends the single-object rule to ordinary class declarations.
challenge.results: The rule attaches to the object definition that uses the template. Its scope supplies no general instance-count rule for classes or JVM programs.

limitations: This is the object-definition construct. An arbitrary class declaration or shared JVM runtime does not establish the same single-object behavior.
Scala 2.13 language-level object definitions. Runtime cardinality across class loaders and compiler lowering require their own evidence.
